A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cl- induced tension transient appears to be mediated via a transverse tube-sarcoplasm reticulum mechanism, while the caffeine- induced transient is mediated via the SR.
the TTs are the site of action for the ionic depolarizing agent, Cl-, and that the TT-SR junction is the site of action of the caffeine receptor.
Ca2+ release from the SR can be stimulated via a mechanism involving TTs, but the mechanism of TT stimulation is not known.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Cl- concentration of the bathing solution is an important determinant of the peak magnitude of the Cl- -stimulated tension transient in the peeled muscle fiber preparation, and that this response may be mediated by the TT-SR system.

the Cl- concentration dependence of the Cl- -stimulated tension transient is consistent with a model in which Ca2+ release occurs via a mechanism that is dependent on a Cl- gradient across the sealed TT membrane.
the Cl- induced tension transient in peeled muscle fibers is not a good model for the depolarization- induced tension transient of intact muscle fibers.
